I give up.

The theorem is a general-n counting result, and I don't think I can finish a sound Lean proof of it in this session.

The math: the condition only constrains points outside S = {1,…,k}. Those points must not lie on a cycle, so the count is the number of rooted forests on n vertices with k fixed roots, times n^k for the values on S. That gives k·n^{n-k-1}·n^k = k·n^{n-1}. Formalizing this needs a Cayley-type forest count, and I found no Prüfer-code or Cayley's-formula result in the installed Mathlib to build on. The obvious induction (delete a non-S point and redirect its preimages) produces a weighted sum over subsets of fibers, which doesn't reduce to the closed form cleanly. Building the bijection from scratch would be a large development, well beyond this task.

I checked that the statement elaborates as expected, and I did not modify `/work/putnam_2013_b5.lean`. It still contains the original `sorry`. I removed my scratch file.
